Directional agreement between GPT and Llama on 616 shared posts: 81.3%.

Figure 1 -- distribution shape (Finding 1)

What to look for: If the third panel shows the entropy gap is largest in the ambiguous stratum, this supports H1b (LLMs collapse to majority answers when humans are genuinely split).

What this run shows: Mean entropy gap on ambiguous posts: gpt=0.598, llama=0.660. Values above zero indicate the LLM's per-scenario distribution is tighter than the human distribution.

Figure 2 -- decision feature heterogeneity (Finding 2a)

What to look for: Look for visibly larger abs_gap in irreversible decisions and in long-horizon decisions. Resource constraint is exploratory; sample sizes per cell vary.

What this run shows: Overall median abs_gap per model: gpt median=0.109, llama median=0.208.

Figure 3 -- SES strain (Finding 2b, binary)

What to look for: Given the heavy skew in the SES distribution, the preregistration update collapses to low vs non-low. If the low bar is meaningfully higher than non-low, that is an early signal for H2c.

What this run shows: gpt: low median=0.146, non-low median=0.105 | llama: low median=0.239, non-low median=0.205

Figure 4 -- cross-model comparison

What to look for: Panel 4b tells you how much new information a third model would add. If GPT and Llama already cluster tightly along the diagonal, Claude is unlikely to change the qualitative picture -- though it is still required for the preregistered confirmatory tests.

What this run shows: Directional agreement between GPT and Llama on 616 shared posts: 81.3%.

Figure 5 -- stability / calibration

What to look for: A well-calibrated model should show entropy that roughly tracks the human consensus level (low entropy where humans agree, higher where humans are split). A flat, consistently low line indicates collapse regardless of human uncertainty.

What this run shows: See per-model median entropy in each consensus stratum. The dashed line at log(2) = 0.693 marks the theoretical maximum for a binary choice.

Should we run Claude Sonnet 4.6?

Heuristics (descriptive, not a stopping rule):

  • If the ambiguous-stratum entropy gap is roughly >0.15 for both models, running Claude is likely worth it.
  • If the reversibility or time_horizon panels show a difference of >0.05 in median abs_gap with the expected sign, running Claude is likely worth it.
  • If GPT and Llama already agree on 90%+ of post-level directions, Claude probably will not move the qualitative picture much, but is still needed for the preregistered confirmatory tests.

Observed values from this run:

  • Ambiguous-stratum mean entropy gap: gpt=0.598, llama=0.660 (avg=0.629). Heuristic >0.15 → likely worth running Claude.
  • GPT-vs-Llama directional agreement: 81.3% across 616 shared posts. >90% means Claude is unlikely to move the qualitative picture, though still required for preregistered tests.
